messages:
oliver: FYI I hit a reproducible parsing oddity in the sample streaming demo that only shows up when the client process is killed with SIGKILL and immediately restarted. node-sdk and python-sdk behave differently.

oliver: Repro (local): start sample stream, send one event WITHOUT final blank-line, kill client with `kill -9 <pid>`, restart client within 50-150ms, send next event. ~10% runs merged previous trailing bytes into the next event.

oliver: tcpdump snip:
```
conn A tail: data: {"m":"one"}
# process exits (no CRLF flush)
conn B head: data: {"m":"two"}
# server sees : data: {"m":"one"}
data: {"m":"two"}
# browser/node parsers differ on whether this becomes 1 or 2 events
```

tara: interesting that SIGKILL specifically spikes it. SIGKILL won't run any atexit flush logic so buffers can be partial. which SDK parsers are we using?

yun: node-sdk uses our lightweight sse-parser that waits for blank-line delimiter to emit. python-sdk's aiohttp client yields events more eagerly when a transport close is observed. So node ends up appending next conn bytes to leftover buffer.

tara: two mitigations: (A) client-side: on socket `close`/`error` force-clear or comment-emit partial buffer, optionally opt-in; (B) server-side: always append explicit `\n\n` and call socket.flush, but that doesn't help if client is SIGKILL before flushing.

yun: agree. I prototyped a small opt-in option `sse.reconnectMode = "truncate-on-close"|"emit-comment"|"legacy"`. Default `legacy` keeps previous behavior. `emit-comment` writes `:partial-truncated` as a comment so JSON parsers ignore it. `truncate-on-close` silently drops partial buffer.

oliver: nice. parity question: will python default to same flag? we should avoid surprising users across SDKs.

yun: proposal: release node and python with same default `legacy` but document opt-in and recommend `emit-comment` for demo/sampleapp. Add an opt-out config env var for demos.

tara: also add a tiny integration test that spawns child process that does `socket.write('data: {"m":"x"}'); process.kill(process.pid, 'SIGKILL')` then new client connects and sends next event. CI can run this on loopback. That caught regressions for me.

oliver: PR opened for node-sdk: https://github.com/redwood-inference/node-sdk/pull/900 (adds the option, unit + integration tests, sampleapp pin). I included a small comment about backwards compatibility.

build-bot: Created issue DEVEX-2333: "sse: SIGKILL leads to partial buffer merge on fast reconnects (node/python parity)" (https://tracker.internal/DEVEX-2333)

yun: one more edge: browsers can't send SIGKILL obviously, but mobile apps that crash can cause similar behavior. so still worth the client fix.

tara: let's also add a short doc blurb under docs/streaming.md recommending: (1) servers flush double-newline after each event, (2) demos use `emit-comment` flag, (3) for production consider `truncate-on-close` only if you can tolerate dropping partials.

oliver: agreed. I'll follow up with a small note in the sampleapp README and a short changelog entry. Thanks for the quick triage everyone.
